**Ida Abelman color artworks in the U.S. GSA Fine Arts Collection that were *not* produced via lithographic print**

| *Countryside* | 1939 | color woodcut | “Medium: color woodcut” (GSA list page 1)【Page note: https://art.gsa.gov/people/829/ida-abelman/objects/list?page=1】 |
| *Countryside* | c. 1935 | color woodcut | “Medium: color woodcut” (GSA list page 2)【Page note: https://art.gsa.gov/people/829/ida-abelman/objects/list?page=2】 |

*Note:* No other Ida Abelman works in the GSA listing indicate a color medium that is not a lithographic print (e.g., “color lithograph” is lithographic and therefore excluded).

**Youngest of these works**

The two works above have dates 1939 and c. 1935; therefore the youngest is the *1939* *Countryside*.

**Westernmost museum that holds the youngest work**

The GSA record for the 1939 *Countryside* is available at ID 11817, which is catalogued as being in the **Weisman Art Museum, Minneapolis, MN**【Page note: https://art.gsa.gov/objects/11817/countryside?ctx=169d736c8779aaa83482e47bdf610f3472619a5a&idx=35】.  
The next nearest GSA holding of a color‑woodcut by Abelman is the 1935 *Countryside* in the **Newark Museum, Newark, NJ**【Page note: https://art.gsa.gov/objects/2275/countryside?ctx=169d736c8779aaa83482e47bdf610f3472619a5a&idx=40】.

Because Minneapolis lies further west than Newark (Minneapolis ≈ −93.6 ° W, Newark ≈ −74.1 ° W), the **Weisman Art Museum in Minneapolis, MN** is the westernmost museum that holds the youngest Ida Abelman color artwork (the 1939 *Countryside*) in the U.S. GSA Fine Arts Collection.
